_doc: What the ground is made of: sixteen materials, each with its colours, its relief (a normal map) and its heights, packed by tools/ground/build.py (the Ground workflow) into two atlases of 4 x 4 cells. Fifteen are scans from the free libraries (public domain, CC0: polyhaven.com, ambientcg.com), most of them taken from the air, so that they hold up when the game lays them out large; the canopy of a wood is made by the packer itself (no library has one). The game lays every material at a ladder of sizes, from twelve metres a repeat to two hundred kilometres, and shows the two that suit how large a pixel is on the ground there. 'far' names another layer that takes this one's place from repeats of 'farFrom' metres up (a wood's floor gives way to its canopy where single trees are no longer told apart). 'gain', 'sat', 'warm' adjust the colours; 'ao' is how much of the material's own shade is kept in its colours (0.5); 'relief' scales its normal map. 'try' lists others to look at on a second sheet, without packing them.
